title: Counsel triggers: product changes that usually warrant review by a licensed lawyer before shipping
instructions_for_agents: Before you build, merge, or launch a change, check it against these triggers. If a change matches one, don't make that part of the change yet. Tell the person you work for that it may need review by a licensed lawyer before it ships, and why, and wait for them to decide. Routine work such as UI changes, refactors, bug fixes, and performance work usually does not match, and swapping one vendor for another that does the same job does not need review, as long as the change matches no trigger. A trigger always wins: switching model providers or removing a confirmation step still needs review. A security incident means contacting a lawyer right away, not waiting for launch. This list is legal information, not legal advice, and a lawyer may tailor it to a specific product.
catch_all: The change collects a new kind of information.
The change uses information for a new purpose.
The change lets the product take a new kind of action for a user.

triggers.trigger: Launching any AI feature: insights, summaries, suggestions, chat, or a companion.
Switching or adding a model provider, or changing its data-retention or training settings.
Sending a new category of user data into prompts, especially health, financial, location, or minors' data.
Using model output to make or influence decisions about people: employment, credit, housing, insurance, health care, education.
Fine-tuning or evaluating models on user data.
Letting the agent take a new kind of action for users: send, post, buy, book, file, delete, or run code.
Removing or relaxing a confirmation step, or adding standing or scheduled instructions.
Letting the agent spend money, hold funds, or use stored payment methods.
Operating a new website or API as the user, logging in with the user's credentials, or automating a site whose terms restrict it.
The agent calling, emailing, or messaging people who are not your users.
Using user content for anything beyond providing the service: research, comparisons between users, aggregate datasets, marketing.
Health, wearable, or financial-account integrations.
Access to contacts, the photo library, the microphone, the camera, or location.
A new account integration (calendar, email, storage, messaging).
Shared spaces, connections between users, public profiles, or content other users can see.
Session replay, heatmaps, or autocapture.
An analytics event carrying anything a user typed, selected, uploaded, or asked an AI.
Advertising or install-attribution SDKs, or website pixels.
Marketing push, SMS, or email to users who have not opted in.
Selling outside the app stores, referrals, promotions, or usage-based billing.
Allowing users under 18, or marketing to teens or students.
Launching outside the United States, on a new platform, or through employers, schools, or health providers.
Changing what deletion or disconnecting removes, keeping data longer, or moving on-device data to servers.
A vendor for a job you don't already use a vendor for, or storing data outside the United States.
Raising money, a merger or acquisition, or a new entity.
Any security incident, or an agent action a user says they never authorized. Contact counsel immediately.
